name: Kuk Swamp banana cultivation
description: At Kuk Swamp in the New Guinea highlands, banana phytoliths occur in agricultural features and are interpreted as evidence for cultivation of Musa acuminata derivatives.

date.label: Approximately 6950–6440 cal BP (5000–4490 BCE)
date.basis: Source-reported period or approximate chronology; where calibrated BP is stated, converted using the 1950 reference epoch.

events.statement: At Kuk Swamp in the New Guinea highlands, banana phytoliths occur in agricultural features and are interpreted as evidence for cultivation of Musa acuminata derivatives.
events.caveats: Cultivation is inferred from associated features and diagnostic plant remains, not a direct observation of planting; the chronology and species identifications remain subject to archaeological interpretation. The paper text gives 6950–6440 cal BP for the agricultural feature fills, while its figure caption gives 6990–6440 for one sample. A 2011 regional synthesis proposes complex domestication and possible westward dispersal, but does not trace a specific subsequent site to these individual Kuk remains.

evidence.supports: The authors date pertinent feature fills to 6950–6440 cal BP; rare phytoliths match M. acuminata and occur in an agricultural context.

evidence.locator: Bananas and conclusions, pp. S387–S388, S391
evidence.supports: The review describes a regionally complex history of banana domestication and cultivation inferred from phytoliths and features at Kuk. It discusses evidence suggestive of westward dispersal from the New Guinea region, while noting the lack of direct archaeobotanical verification for parts of the proposed route; no direct link from the individual Kuk assemblage is established.
